identity.name: First-Time Kubernetes Secret Enumeration & Access (SIM-CDR-026)
identity.summary: A Kubernetes service account that never touched the secrets API in baseline lists all secrets in its namespace and then reads them, the enumerate-then-harvest shape of container-API credential theft. The k8s_audit_emitter streams shape-true audit.k8s.io/v1 audit records (list/get secrets) into kubernetes_audit_logs so XSIAM's ML secret-access analytics fire.
identity.description: Exercises the two XSIAM Kubernetes-audit ML analytics alerts 'Kubernetes secrets enumeration for the first time' and 'Unusual Kubernetes secret access'. Both are behavioral/ML detections that learn per-identity secret-access baselines from the Kubernetes API-server audit feed and flag a previously-unseen subject enumerating and then reading secrets — the credential-access precursor to lateral movement in a cluster. Signal is generated by the k8s_audit_emitter analytics log-streamer (a get/list secrets burst by an out-of-baseline service account), so no real cluster is touched.

prerequisites.description: An operator-supplied HTTP collector already wired into Cortex XSIAM as a Kubernetes-audit (kubernetes_audit_logs) third-party source, and reachable from the jumpbox running the EAL CLI.

payload.code:
# Drive the k8s_audit_emitter analytics log-streamer to emit a first-time
# secrets enumeration burst then an unusual secret read for a service account
# that never touched the secrets API in baseline. All records are shape-true
# audit.k8s.io/v1 Events POSTed to the operator's collector (kubernetes_audit_logs).
set -euo pipefail
python3 -m scripts.eal_simulator.cli run /tmp/cdr-026-enum.yml --live
python3 -m scripts.eal_simulator.cli run /tmp/cdr-026-access.yml --live

input_variables.name: COLLECTOR_URL
input_variables.description: Operator-supplied HTTP collector wired into XSIAM as the kubernetes_audit_logs source.

expected_artifacts.description: Kubernetes API-server audit records: verb=list then verb=get on objectRef.resource=secrets by an out-of-baseline service account.

abiocs.name: Kubernetes secrets enumeration for the first time
abiocs.description: Analytics (first-seen ML): a Kubernetes identity lists secrets for the first time. XSIAM learns which service accounts enumerate secrets in baseline; a previously-unseen subject issuing a list-secrets call is flagged as reconnaissance. This is a first-seen anomaly over the API-server audit feed, not a parent->child causality-chain ABIOC. Keyed on the kubernetes_audit_logs API-server audit feed.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = kubernetes_audit_logs
| filter verb = "list" and objectRef_resource = "secrets"
| filter user_username = "system:serviceaccount:cortexsim-canary:compromised-sa"
| comp count() as enum_events by user_username, sourceIPs, objectRef_namespace
| filter enum_events >= 1
| fields user_username, sourceIPs, objectRef_namespace, enum_events
abiocs.causality_anchor: Per-service-account secret-enumeration baseline: the set of identities that have historically issued list/watch on the secrets resource. A first-seen subject deviates from that learned baseline.

abiocs.name: Unusual Kubernetes secret access
abiocs.description: Analytics (behavioral / ML): a Kubernetes identity reads secrets in a way that deviates from its established access baseline. XSIAM learns typical per-identity secret get/watch behavior from the API-server audit feed and flags atypical reads (new secrets, new source IP, or a spike in volume). Keyed on kubernetes_audit_logs.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = kubernetes_audit_logs
| filter verb in ("get", "watch") and objectRef_resource = "secrets"
| filter user_username = "system:serviceaccount:cortexsim-canary:compromised-sa"
| comp count() as secret_reads by user_username, sourceIPs, objectRef_name
| filter secret_reads >= 1
| fields user_username, sourceIPs, objectRef_name, secret_reads
abiocs.causality_anchor: Per-service-account secret-read baseline: the secrets, source IPs, and access rate a given identity normally touches. Reading a secret outside that learned profile is the deviation.

xql_queries.name: Kubernetes secret audit records observed for the run window
xql_queries.query:
dataset = kubernetes_audit_logs
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter objectRef_resource = "secrets" and verb in ("get", "list", "watch")
| comp count() as observed_audit_records by user_username, verb
| filter observed_audit_records >= 1
| fields user_username, verb, observed_audit_records

correlation_rules.name: SIM-CDR-026 first-time enumerate-then-harvest secret theft
correlation_rules.logic: Fires when analytics alert `Kubernetes secrets enumeration for the first time` and analytics alert `Unusual Kubernetes secret access` both observe the same user_username (Kubernetes service account) from the same sourceIPs within a 10-minute window, stitching the first-seen enumeration and the anomalous read into one CDR credential-theft incident.

analytics_modules.module: Kubernetes secrets enumeration for the first time
analytics_modules.note: Backed by the first-seen Analytics detection on this card and driven by the k8s_audit_emitter secret_enumeration preset (documented as an Analytics alert in the plugin preset->alert map).
Backed by the behavioral Analytics detection on this card and driven by the k8s_audit_emitter secret_access preset (documented as an Analytics alert in the plugin preset->alert map).

products.evidence_query: dataset = kubernetes_audit_logs | filter objectRef_resource = "secrets" and verb in ("get", "list", "watch") | comp count() as n by user_username, verb | fields user_username, verb, n

threat_scenarios.name: First-time Kubernetes secret enumeration & access
threat_scenarios.description: Validate that XSIAM's ML Kubernetes-audit analytics detect an out-of-baseline service account enumerating and reading secrets — the container-API credential-theft precursor to cluster lateral movement.

threat_steps.objective: First-time secret enumeration by an out-of-baseline service account raises the first-seen Analytics alert.
preconditions: A collector wired into XSIAM as the kubernetes_audit_logs source.
steps: Run the k8s_audit_emitter secret_enumeration preset against the collector.
Observe the `Kubernetes secrets enumeration for the first time` Analytics alert fire.
success_criteria: Analytics alert `Kubernetes secrets enumeration for the first time` fires for the service account within the run window.

threat_steps.objective: The subsequent secret read raises the unusual-access Analytics alert and the correlation stitches both into one incident.
preconditions: TS-CDR-026A enumeration observed for the same service account.
steps: Run the k8s_audit_emitter secret_access preset for the same identity.
Observe the `Unusual Kubernetes secret access` Analytics alert and correlation `CR-CDR-0026`.
success_criteria: Analytics alert `Unusual Kubernetes secret access` fires and correlation `CR-CDR-0026` raises one incident.

preventive_controls: Scope service-account RBAC to least privilege — deny list/get on the secrets resource unless a workload genuinely needs it.
Prefer projected/short-lived tokens and external secret stores (CSI Secrets Store) over long-lived Kubernetes Secret objects.
Enable and forward the API-server audit log at RequestResponse level for the secrets resource to XSIAM.
detection_engineering: Baseline which service accounts touch the secrets API and alert on first-seen enumerators.
Correlate a first-time list-secrets with a subsequent get on the same identity/source IP within a short window.
